result:
CALM-3 (round 232) is implemented and all my checks pass, but I've written one STOP at the top of `a-round-232.md` that B needs to rule on.

**The STOP:** an existing render-budget test ("does not re-render clips, overview bars…") is now above half of its 5-second default timeout when the 32 covering test files run together: 2.59–2.79 s (52–56 %). At gate 231 it took 1.75 s. On its own it takes 1.45 s. As a control I re-ran the same files with the old app code put back temporarily, and it took 2.57 s. So the slowdown comes from load on this machine, not from this change. The rule (L32) still requires a STOP. I didn't touch the test because its file is frozen. It passes every time. B can accept the variance, grant a timeout on it, or split it. The report says plainly that this is not an implementation stop, so C should run the full round.

**What changed:** exactly the 8 permitted files plus the 4 new ones. Protected auth, purchase and download files are unchanged, and the frozen and root-owned files still match their recorded hashes.
- In an empty project the Overview is now a quiet 1 px line; its frame and playhead are hidden.
- Ctrl+Alt+O (Cmd+Option+O on Mac) hides and shows it. The browser remembers the choice, and while it's hidden an empty space of the same size keeps the layout from moving.
- The status line confirms each toggle, and the shortcut sheet lists the key.
- The video caption row lost its unneeded spacing classes (GATE229-S2).
- Implementation doc 180 is written.

The app changes are B's reference diff, applied unchanged. I wrote the real tests: the main test file has 6 cases, and the remembered-choice case has its own file so stored state can't leak between tests.

**Checks I ran:**
- Typecheck and lint pass; 0 lint findings in the files I own.
- The 32-file covering set passes, 541 tests, three times. The two new test files also pass in random order.
- Deliberate-bug checks: 7 of the 8 planned ones make a test fail. The eighth (frame not hidden) can only be seen in a browser, as the task expected. I added one more for the pointer-drag guard, which also fails as it should.
- I ran B's browser probe against the running server on :5173. All 440 measured values match B's run exactly, with 0 page errors.

**Code review:** the code-reviewer agent found no Blocker or Medium issues and five Lows. I fixed three in my own test files: the pointer-drag guard had no test, the server-render case hid console errors too widely, and the held-key case didn't check that the key was blocked. Its architecture note goes to B with no action this round. It says to keep the keyboard handler and the two storage helpers as they are, and proposes one shared setup helper for the workspace tests.

**Known gaps:**
- The visual empty state, the focus ring and any flash before the page finishes loading can only be checked by C in the browser.
- The Mac shortcut needs a real Mac.
- One storage-error test only reaches the failing-read path if it runs first; it does prove the failing-write path.
- A toggle in another tab only shows here after reload.
- Firefox's handling of AltGr is unverified.

I claimed none of C's acceptance rows, made no commits, and didn't start or stop any server. The report also lists the exact next checks for C.

Files are in `/home/runner/czaba-project/tmp/studio-real-loop`:
- a-round-232.md
- a-round-232/granted-hunks.diff
- a-round-232/changed-end-sha256.txt
